microtheory.name: reflective_codegen_axiom3
microtheory.definition: L5 composition pattern — reflective access (Paper 1 Axiom 3) + codegen surface. Composed of: Γ represented as a subgraph of G; Π operations that observe + extend Γ from within G; Term-trees as the JIT's codegen input; a chosen backend (substrate_rs uses dynasm-rs); safepoint polling at loop back-edges + call sites; OSR-based deoptimisation to the interpreter; inline caches per dispatch site; method JIT in v1, tracing JIT named as future alternative; finite-depth reflective tower with lazy materialisation. Bridges to adaptive_tiered_dispatch (L2) via shared gamma_epoch + the TierUp → compile → install loop. Each piece exists in other Mts (compilers' tiered_compilation + OSR + inline_cache + tracing_JIT; reflection_metaprogramming's grammar_as_data + reflective_tower + intercession; paper1 Axiom 3); this Mt names how they compose for the L5 reflective + codegen layer.

concepts.name: reflective_codegen_axiom3_pattern
concepts.definition: The composition pattern. Γ is a subgraph of G; mutating Γ goes through Substrate::add_production (which bumps gamma_epoch); rules + productions have Term-tree where-clauses that the JIT compiles to native x86_64 via dynasm-rs; compiled fragments installed in the L2 dispatcher's cache keyed by kind (Sym); inline caches per dispatch site avoid repeat lookups; safepoint polls at loop back-edges + before calls; guard failures or epoch-stale hits trigger OSR back to the interpreter; tower materialised to a finite default depth with deeper levels lazy.

concepts.name: gamma_as_graph_subgraph
concepts.definition: Component 1. Productions + rewrite rules are graph data in G — they have node types (Production, Rule), attributes, and edges. Π operations like Substrate::add_production + Substrate::add_rule are the canonical mutators. Per Paper 1 Axiom 3: 'G's own structure — including Γ itself — is representable as a subgraph of G.' Substrate analogue: substrate's Grammar + rules.

concepts.name: operations_on_gamma_from_pi
concepts.definition: Component 2. Π (the mutation surface) includes operations that not only observe but MODIFY Γ from within G. add_production, add_rule, delete_rule (planned). Each Γ mutation bumps gamma_epoch — the bridge to L2's cache invalidation surface. Without this, Γ would be frozen at startup and the substrate couldn't self-modify.

concepts.name: term_tree_as_codegen_input
concepts.definition: Component 3. The JIT's input is a Term-tree (TermIdx + TermArena) — kernel arithmetic + comparison + control flow + graph access. Term-trees are graph-resident (a Term is a Concept). Substrate analogue: jit.rs::compile takes &TermArena + TermIdx + &FxHashMap<Sym, u32> var-indices.

concepts.name: dynasm_x86_backend_v1
concepts.definition: Component 4. substrate_rs uses dynasm-rs as the runtime assembler for x86_64. dynasm provides macros emitting bytes at Rust compile time; the substrate walks the Term-tree at runtime calling those macros. Falls back to interpreter for Terms the JIT doesn't handle. Alternatives named in tradeoffs: Cranelift (more portable, slower compile), LLVM ORC (most optimisation, heaviest), inkwell (LLVM bindings).

concepts.name: inline_cache_per_callsite
concepts.definition: Component 5. Per dispatch site, an inline cache maps observed kind → resolved compiled artefact pointer. Avoids the per-call HashMap lookup once the site stabilises. Mono → poly → mega tier transitions. V8's PIC + HotSpot's IC are the reference. Substrate analogue: not yet implemented at the callsite level; AdaptiveDispatcher's CodeCache is the global equivalent.

concepts.name: tracing_vs_method_jit_choice
concepts.definition: Component 6. Method JIT compiles whole rule where-clauses; tracing JIT compiles hot paths through them (loop bodies, common branches). substrate_rs uses method JIT for v1 (jit.rs is whole-Term-tree). Tracing is named as a future variant for rules with predictable inner loops (audio frames).

concepts.name: safepoint_polling_at_yield
concepts.definition: Component 7. JIT'd code emits safepoint polls at loop back-edges + before calls. Each safepoint carries a map: native PC → interpreter Term-tree position + live variable layout. Guard failures or epoch-mismatch hits trigger OSR through the nearest safepoint. WITHOUT THIS, deoptimisation cannot reconstruct interpreter state, violating correctness_via_interpreter_fallback.

concepts.name: osr_state_reconstruction
concepts.definition: Component 8. On stack replacement. At a safepoint, the runtime unwinds the JIT'd frame + reconstructs the interpreter's state (Term-tree position + variable bindings) + resumes interpretation. Realises the deoptimisation_on_stack_replacement component of executable_memory_lifecycle + adaptive_tiered_dispatch's bounded_deopt_amortised_cost invariant.

concepts.name: tier_up_via_l2_dispatch
concepts.definition: Component 9. The bridge to L2-dynamic. AdaptiveDispatcher::submit returns DispatchOutcome::TierUp when a kind crosses the threshold; an L5 compile pass responds: compile the rule's Term-tree via jit::compile, install via dispatcher.install_compiled. The L2 + L5 patterns interlock through this hand-off.

concepts.name: metacircular_interpreter
concepts.definition: Component 10. The interpreter that evaluates Term-trees is itself expressible IN Γ — its own evaluation rules could be rewritten as Γ productions. This is the deep Axiom 3 commitment: NO part of the substrate is outside the substrate's own reflective scope. substrate_rs's interpreter is in Rust currently; the meta-circular ascent to evaluator-as-graph is future work.

concepts.name: tower_finite_with_lazy_depth
concepts.definition: Component 11. Smith's reflective tower is in principle infinite; in practice every system materialises a finite default depth + makes deeper levels lazy. substrate_rs default: 3 levels (object level + meta + meta-meta). Deeper instances materialise only when a reflex explicitly reads them.

concepts.name: guard_with_deopt_target
concepts.definition: Component 12. JIT'd code emits guards before assumed-type accesses (e.g. 'assume attr is Int'). On guard failure, branch to the deopt target for the enclosing safepoint. The guard is a single compare + branch; deopt cost is amortised across the assumed-path acceleration.

concepts.name: axiom3_via_gamma_subgraph
concepts.definition: Invariant. Γ representable as G subgraph; Π operations on Γ from within G. Honoured by storing productions + rules in the graph and mutating via Substrate::add_production / add_rule. Without this, Axiom 3 is only structurally claimed, not operationally realised.

concepts.name: interpreter_correct_by_construction
concepts.definition: Invariant. The Term-tree interpreter walks the canonical structure + always produces the correct value. The JIT is an acceleration; deoptimisation always lands on the interpreter. No execution path bypasses interpreter correctness. (Same as adaptive_tiered_dispatch's correctness_via_interpreter_fallback but stated at the codegen-honesty level.)

concepts.name: compiled_code_invalidates_on_gamma_change
concepts.definition: Invariant. Compiled artefacts stamp themselves with epoch_at_compile; lookups check current epoch; mismatch deopts. The bridge through Substrate::gamma_epoch (commit f81559e) ensures Γ mutations propagate from the substrate's mutation surface to the dispatcher's cache invalidation surface.

concepts.name: safepoints_cover_all_yield_points
concepts.definition: Invariant. Every loop back-edge + every call site has a safepoint. Without complete coverage, deopt requested mid-execution may not find a valid reconstruction point — undefined behaviour. The JIT's safepoint insertion is part of the contract.

concepts.name: tower_must_be_finite_in_practice
concepts.definition: Invariant. Materialised tower depth is bounded. Smith's design accepts this — infinite tower is a theoretical limit; practical implementations cap + use lazy materialisation. substrate_rs caps at 3 levels by default.

concepts.name: tradeoff_backend_choice
concepts.definition: Tradeoff: dynasm-rs (Rust-native, simple, x86_64 only, no optimisation passes) vs Cranelift (Wasmtime's backend, multi-arch, fast compile, moderate optimisation) vs LLVM via inkwell (most optimisation, heaviest compile + dependency). substrate_rs picks dynasm for v1; Cranelift planned as a portable alternative.

concepts.name: tradeoff_jit_strategy
concepts.definition: Tradeoff: method JIT (compile whole where-clause; substrate v1) vs tracing JIT (compile hot path; LuaJIT-style) vs meta-tracing (compile interpreter under JIT; PyPy-style). substrate picks method for simplicity + the Term-tree input shape.

concepts.name: tradeoff_safepoint_density
concepts.definition: Tradeoff: dense safepoints (lower deopt latency, slower JIT'd code) vs sparse safepoints (faster code, slower deopt). substrate's default: at every loop back-edge + before each call. Tunable per kind.

concepts.name: tradeoff_ic_size
concepts.definition: Tradeoff: monomorphic-only IC (smallest, fastest, frequent megamorphic fall-through) vs mono + poly (handles common polymorphism, slightly larger) vs mono + poly + mega (handles full polymorphism, largest cache). V8 picks all three tiers; substrate_rs starts with mono.

concepts.name: tradeoff_tower_materialisation
concepts.definition: Tradeoff: eager materialisation (full tower available, large startup memory) vs lazy (small startup, latency hit on deep introspection). substrate_rs picks lazy with 3-level default eager.

concepts.name: substrate_rs_canonical_instance
concepts.definition: substrate_rs as canonical instance. jit.rs (commit history pre-this-Mt) compiles Term-trees to native x86_64 via dynasm-rs; l2_adaptive (commits 6783650 + 13b84a4) routes TierUp signals to compile passes; code_cache (commit f1f376f) holds JittedFn behind Arc; l2_jit_integration tests (commit e5ba8d5) verify the loop end-to-end. Deferred: safepoint maps, OSR state reconstruction, inline caches at callsites, tracing JIT.

concepts.name: hotspot_c1_c2_reference
concepts.definition: Java HotSpot's tiered compilation. C1 fast-but-less-optimised compile, C2 slower-but-fully-optimised. Profile-driven; OSR for tier-up inside hot loops; safepoint polls at backward branches + method returns. Influential reference for tier_up_via_l2_dispatch + safepoint_polling_at_yield.

concepts.name: v8_turbofan_reference
concepts.definition: V8's TurboFan (current optimising tier). Sea-of-nodes IR; speculative optimisation with deopt support; polymorphic inline caches. Reference for inline_cache_per_callsite + guard_with_deopt_target.

concepts.name: luajit_trace_reference
concepts.definition: LuaJIT's trace JIT. Compiles hot loops as linear traces; side exits to interpreter on guard fail. Reference for tradeoff_jit_strategy (tracing alternative) + minimal-overhead guard pattern.

concepts.name: pypy_meta_tracing_reference
concepts.definition: PyPy's meta-tracing. Trace through the interpreter itself + specialise to the executed program. Closest analogue to the substrate's Axiom-3 claim (the interpreter IS Π, observable as Γ subgraph). Reference for metacircular_interpreter.

concepts.name: cranelift_wasmtime_reference
concepts.definition: Cranelift's compiler IR (used by Wasmtime). Fast compile, moderate optimisation, multi-architecture. Reference for tradeoff_backend_choice's portable alternative.

concepts.name: smith_3_lisp_reference
concepts.definition: Brian Cantwell Smith's 3-LISP. The reference reflective tower implementation. Lazily materialised meta-levels; eval-quote symmetry. Reference for tower_finite_with_lazy_depth + the theoretical foundation of operations_on_gamma_from_pi.

concepts.name: naming_completes_l5_design
concepts.definition: Meta. Before this Mt, L5 existed only as a DesignLayer node from the runner-design walk + as gestures in l2_adaptive's docs ('reflective_tower'). The components were scattered across reflection_metaprogramming + compilers + jit.rs without a name binding them. This Mt names the composition + identifies the L2 ↔ L5 bridge as `tier_up_via_l2_dispatch`.

concepts.name: this_mt_bridges_l2_to_l5
concepts.definition: Meta. adaptive_tiered_dispatch (L2-dynamic) names the dispatch + cache surface; this Mt names the codegen + reflection surface. The two interlock through TierUp → compile → install. Without naming this bridge, the L2 pattern's tier_up_signal would dangle — there'd be no named recipient.

rules.name: gamma_must_have_g_representation
rules.head: Jabberwock stores a production or rewrite rule
rules.body: the production/rule must be representable as graph data (nodes + edges + attrs) in G. Otherwise Axiom 3's reflective access fails — there'd be parts of the rule store outside the substrate's own introspectable surface.

rules.name: operations_on_gamma_bump_epoch
rules.head: Jabberwock's Π mutates Γ
rules.body: the mutation must bump gamma_epoch with Release ordering. Cached compiled artefacts depending on the prior Γ become stale on the next epoch read. Wired in commit f81559e for add_rule + add_production.

rules.name: tier_up_routes_through_l2
rules.head: Jabberwock's L5 compile pass produces a JittedFn for kind K
rules.body: install via the L2 dispatcher's install_compiled API; the artefact gets stamped with the current epoch + cached. Direct stuffing of compiled code into hand-rolled storage bypasses the L2 cache + breaks invalidation.

rules.name: interpreter_path_always_available
rules.head: Jabberwock has a JIT'd compiled artefact for kind K
rules.body: the corresponding Term-tree interpreter must still be runnable. Deoptimisation requires it. No code path may delete the Term-tree when a JIT'd version is installed.

rules.name: safepoints_at_every_yield
rules.head: Jabberwock's JIT emits code for a Term-tree containing loops or calls
rules.body: each loop back-edge + each call site must have a safepoint poll + safepoint map entry. Without this, deopt at that point has no reconstruction target — undefined behaviour.

rules.name: tower_collapse_after_finite_depth
rules.head: Jabberwock's reflection requires meta-level N where N > default depth
rules.body: the runtime materialises level N on demand (lazy expansion). Materialised tower in practice never grows unbounded. Without a finite cap, reflective recursion would blow the stack on a deep enough query.
